title: Uniformly most split reliable graphs: a complete answer outside two edge counts
oneLine: An existence classification leaves two all-order boundary counts, certifies them through 51 vertices, and controls explicit probability intervals at every order.
abstract: This unrefereed mathematical candidate studies connected simple graphs whose independently retained edges must form exactly two components, one per designated terminal. For n at least seven it proves nonexistence of uniform maximisers in an intermediate edge range and existence in the dense range, leaving two boundary edge counts conditional at unrestricted orders. Exact cone-reliability certificates resolve those counts through n = 51. Analytic cone comparisons cover p at least one half and an explicit interval near zero at every order, without resolving the intervening interval. The result classifies existence, not all optimisers.
evidence: Written analytic arguments and exact finite cone-reliability certificates; all-order interval bounds are distinct from finite full-interval coverage.
statusDetail: Unrefereed AI-assisted candidate. No external peer review, unaffiliated reproduction or proof-assistant formalisation established. Two all-order boundary counts remain conditional.

problem.name: Existence of uniformly most split reliable graphs

keyResults: For n ≥ 7, no uniform maximiser exists for n ≤ m ≤ C(n,2) − n − 1; explicit dense maximisers exist for m ≥ C(n,2) − n + 2.
The two boundary edge counts are certified for 7 ≤ n ≤ 51; at unrestricted orders they remain conditional.
All-order cone comparisons hold for p ≥ 1/2 and on an explicit positive interval near zero; the intermediate interval remains unresolved.

narration: When one split-network design wins. An Evidence Press briefing. Imagine a network whose links survive independently. Success here does not mean keeping everyone connected. It means exactly two connected groups, with one designated terminal in each and no third group. For a fixed number of vertices and edges, can one design maximise that success probability at every link-survival rate? This candidate gives an almost complete existence classification for networks with at least seven vertices. Trees have a uniformly best design, as earlier work established. A substantial intermediate range has none. Sufficiently dense networks have an explicit best construction. Having no uniform winner does not mean there is no best design at a particular survival rate. Two boundary edge counts remain conditional in general. Exact integer certificates settle both for networks from seven through fifty-one vertices. That finite conclusion is separate from a new all-order comparison: it works when links survive with probability at least one half, and on an explicit interval near zero, but leaves the middle unresolved. The proof connects split reliability to ordinary connectivity after identifying the terminals. Endpoint comparisons then reveal when one design cannot win everywhere. The package includes the written arguments and exact checking programs. It does not classify every optimiser or establish external peer review, independent reproduction or formal verification. This is an anonymous, AI-assisted, unrefereed mathematical candidate. Released on eighteen October twenty twenty-six, its paper and reproducible evidence are linked on the Evidence Press release page. This briefing uses an AI-generated voice and is not additional scientific evidence.

corrections.summary: Corrected a structural description in §4.3 and in the explanation of Definition 4.4. The archived text says the extremal graph is C_{n−1}(n−3−ε) “with a pendant vertex attached to a clique vertex”. For ε = 1 the pendant is attached to the cone vertex u, the unique vertex of minimum degree. The text should read: “with a pendant vertex attached to a vertex of minimum degree (the cone vertex u when ε = 1; u or its non-neighbour when ε = 0)”, and Definition 4.4 should note that the right side has the same reliability as the balloon, because a pendant edge contributes the factor p wherever it is attached.
corrections.detail: Reliability does not depend on where the pendant edge is attached. No theorem, certificate, computation or stated result is affected. The archived PDF, version DOI and repository tag are unchanged; the erratum is recorded here and in the repository's CORRECTIONS.md on its main branch.
